Based on the image provided, it appears that "that" refers to the jet flying in the sky. A jet is a type of aircraft that uses jet engines to generate thrust and propel itself through the air. Jet engines work by using the principles of aerodynamics and thermodynamics to produce a high-velocity exhaust gas that generates a reaction force, which in turn propels the aircraft forward.

In the context of science, the study of jet engines and aircraft is closely related to the fields of aerospace engineering and physics. Aerospace engineers design and develop aircraft, spacecraft, and missiles, while physicists study the fundamental laws of motion, energy, and matter that govern the behavior of these vehicles.

To better understand how jet engines work, let's consider a simple analogy. Imagine holding a balloon and then releasing it, allowing it to fly across the room. As the air rushes out of the balloon, it creates a high-pressure region behind it and a low-pressure region in front of it. This pressure difference creates a force that propels the balloon forward. Similarly, a jet engine works by using the energy released from burning fuel to accelerate a large mass of air out of the back of the engine, creating a high-velocity exhaust gas that generates a reaction force that propels the aircraft forward.
